zebralogic.title: RelativeOrdering
zebralogic.principle: When a clue says X is somewhere to the left (or right) of Y, enforce that X's house index is less (or greater) than Y's index.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue mentions a non‑adjacent left/right relationship without specifying distance.
zebralogic.example: A clue states "the master is somewhere to the left of the BMW owner" but the model places the master to the right, violating the ordering.

zebralogic.title: EquivalenceLinking
zebralogic.principle: When a clue equates two attribute values (e.g., "the associate degree holder owns the Toyota Camry"), link those two attributes to the same house.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue directly states that two descriptors refer to the same entity.
zebralogic.example: The model treats "associate degree" and "Toyota Camry" as separate houses, breaking the equivalence.

zebralogic.title: FixedHouseAssignment
zebralogic.principle: If a clue fixes an attribute to a specific house number, enforce that exact placement as a hard constraint.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue mentions a house number (e.g., "Bob is in the third house").
zebralogic.example: Bob is declared to be in house 3, but the model puts him in house 2.

zebralogic.title: CompactFinalAnswer
zebralogic.principle: The solution JSON must be the very last part of the response with no extra characters after it; otherwise the verifier may miss or truncate the answer.
zebralogic.example: The model prints explanatory text after the JSON, causing the verifier to ignore the solution.

zebralogic.title: NegativeHouseAssignment
zebralogic.principle: When a clue explicitly forbids an attribute from being in a particular house, enforce that the attribute cannot occupy that house.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue says "X is not in house Y" or similar negative placement.
zebralogic.example: A clue states the water drinker is not in house 1, yet the model places Eric (water) in house 1.

zebralogic.title: TransitiveEquivalencePropagation
zebralogic.principle: When multiple equivalence clues form a chain (A = B and B = C), propagate the equivalence so all involved attributes share the same house.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When two or more equivalence statements share a variable.
zebralogic.example: A = B and B = C are given, but the model only links A to B, leaving C separate.

zebralogic.title: ExactAttributeValueMatching
zebralogic.principle: Copy attribute values exactly as they appear in the problem statement, preserving spelling, case, and punctuation.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When writing the final JSON, use the exact strings from the attribute list.
zebralogic.example: The clue uses "hip‑hop" but the attribute list contains "hip hop"; the model outputs "hip‑hop", causing a mismatch.

zebralogic.title: LimitReasoningLength
zebralogic.principle: Keep reasoning concise enough to stay within the model's token budget; avoid overly verbose explanations that risk truncation.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When the puzzle has many clues and the output approaches the token limit.
zebralogic.example: The model writes a long paragraph and the verifier truncates before the JSON appears.

zebralogic.title: HouseDistance
zebralogic.principle: When a clue specifies a concrete number of houses between X and Y, enforce that there are exactly that many houses separating them.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue says "There are N houses between X and Y".
zebralogic.example: The model interprets "two houses between" as "two houses apart", placing the items only one house apart.

zebralogic.title: DirectAdjacencyConstraint
zebralogic.principle: When a clue says X is directly left (or right) of Y, enforce that X's house index is exactly one less (or greater) than Y's; there must be zero houses between them.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue contains phrases like "directly left of", "directly right of", "immediately left of", or "immediately right of".
zebralogic.example: A clue states "the tulips are directly left of the Tesla owner" but the model places tulips two houses away, violating adjacency.

zebralogic.description: Misinterpreting 'N houses between' as 'N houses apart'
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model treats the phrase as a simple distance of N instead of interpreting it as N houses separating the two items (i.e., a gap of N+1 positions).
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: When a clue says "there are N houses between X and Y", enforce |pos(X) − pos(Y)| = N + 1.

zebralogic.description: Placing the solution JSON before the end of the response or adding excessive text after it, causing the verifier to miss the answer
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model continues to generate commentary after the JSON or inserts the JSON earlier, so the verifier cannot locate the final answer block.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Output the JSON as the very last token sequence of the response, with no preceding or trailing characters.

zebralogic.description: Exceeding token limit causing the verifier to truncate
zebralogic.why_it_happens: Lengthy reasoning pushes the output past the model's maximum token window, so the tail (including the JSON) gets cut off.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Limit the amount of intermediate reasoning; keep explanations concise and prioritize the final JSON.

zebralogic.description: Ignoring negative house constraints (placing an attribute in a house that a clue explicitly forbids)
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model treats negative statements as optional rather than hard constraints, allowing prohibited placements.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Treat any "not in" or "cannot be" clause as a hard exclusion when building the assignment.

zebralogic.why_it_happens: After extensive reasoning the model forgets to emit the required JSON block, or the generation ends before reaching it.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Reserve the last line of the response for the JSON and explicitly signal "Final answer:" followed immediately by the JSON, with no additional text.
